# Plugging a custom claim producer into a deployment

A claim producer implements five gRPC verbs — capabilities, Open, Commit,
Abandon, Release — and the deployment names it in configuration. What the
producer advertises at startup is what the operator sees; what it returns on
Open is what the node's executor receives.

## Name the producers

```yaml
persistence:
  driver: sqlite
  sqlite:
    path: /var/lib/rimsky/state.db
claim_producers:
  "sync-producer":
    endpoint: "grpc://sync-producer:9411"
    write_semantics_allowed: ["sync"]
  "staged-producer":
    endpoint: "grpc://staged-producer:9412"
    write_semantics_allowed: ["staged_async"]
  "blocking-producer":
    endpoint: "grpc://blocking-producer:9413"
    write_semantics_allowed: ["blocking_async"]
  "readonly-producer":
    endpoint: "grpc://readonly-producer:9414"
    write_semantics_allowed: ["read_only"]
  "scarce":
    endpoint: "grpc://scarce:9415"
    write_semantics_allowed: ["sync"]
named_locks: {}
executors: {}
```

There is no second registration step.

## The advertisement reaches the deployment

```bash
curl -sS "$BASE/v1/observability/claim-producers"
```

Every producer appears, each carrying the error classes it declared in its
capabilities response. What the author puts in the handshake is what an operator
reads off the deployment.

## One node per write semantics

```yaml
name: custom-producer-semantics
version: v1
nodes:
  - type: sync-writer
    executor: http-node
    claim_producers:
      - name: sync-producer
        selector: "/regions/{{params.region}}"
        intent: rw
        alias: held
        data:
          lease_hint: sync
    error_types:
      "acquire/unavailable": {action: give_up}
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          url:    {type: string, default: "http://recorder:19419/rec/sync-writer"}
          method: {type: string, default: POST}
          held_addr:   {type: string, source: "{{claim.held.address}}"}
          held_scope:  {type: string, source: "{{claim.held.claim_scope}}"}
          held_region: {type: string, source: "{{claim.held.payload.region}}"}

  - type: staged-writer
    executor: http-node
    claim_producers:
      - name: staged-producer
        selector: /staged-area
        intent: rw
        alias: held
    error_types:
      "acquire/unavailable": {action: give_up}
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          url:       {type: string, default: "http://recorder:19419/rec/staged-writer"}
          method:    {type: string, default: POST}
          held_addr: {type: string, source: "{{claim.held.address}}"}

  - type: blocking-writer
    executor: http-node
    claim_producers:
      - name: blocking-producer
        selector: /blocking-area
        intent: rw
        alias: held
    error_types:
      "acquire/unavailable": {action: give_up}
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          url:       {type: string, default: "http://recorder:19419/rec/blocking-writer"}
          method:    {type: string, default: POST}
          held_addr: {type: string, source: "{{claim.held.address}}"}

  - type: readonly-reader
    executor: http-node
    claim_producers:
      - name: readonly-producer
        selector: /catalog
        intent: r
        alias: held
    error_types:
      "acquire/unavailable": {action: give_up}
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          url:       {type: string, default: "http://recorder:19419/rec/readonly-reader"}
          method:    {type: string, default: POST}
          held_addr: {type: string, source: "{{claim.held.address}}"}
```

```bash
rimsky instance create "$TPL" --params '{"region":"us-east-1"}' --endpoint "$BASE" -o json
curl -sS -X POST "$BASE/v1/instances/$IID/messages" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -H "Idempotency-Key: wake-$IID" -d '{"type":""}'
rimsky instance nodes "$IID" --endpoint "$BASE" -o json
```

All four nodes settle fresh.

## What the producer receives on Open

The producer's Open request arrives already resolved against the instance. A
template declaring `/regions/{{params.region}}` reaches the producer as
`/regions/us-east-1`. Alongside it come the declared `intent`, the declared
`alias`, and the node's `data` blob byte-for-byte as the template wrote it —
rimsky does not read it.

An author writes against concrete values and carries their own configuration
through the blob untouched, rather than re-implementing substitution inside
their producer.

## What the node's dispatch receives back

Whatever the producer returned on Open arrives in the node's resolved
attributes: the address (`sync-producer://regions/us-east-1`), the claim-scope
bytes, and any named field of the payload the producer synthesized
(`{{claim.held.payload.region}}`).

The producer's return value is the node's input. An author puts store-specific
detail — a connection string, a staging location, a row payload — in front of
the executor without the template author knowing anything about the store.

## Every write semantics closes the same way

```bash
curl -sS "$BASE/v1/observability/claim-handles?limit=100"
```

The persisted claim handles record each producer's realized semantics — `sync`,
`staged_async`, `blocking_async`, `read_only`, one per producer — and all four
reach state `committed`. The write claim closes with a Commit, and so does the
read-intent claim. Any of the four gets the same lifecycle guarantee.

## A producer's own refusal reaches the template

A producer that answers Open with `Unavailable` carrying the error class it
declares:

```yaml
name: custom-producer-unavailable
version: v1
nodes:
  - type: waiting-writer
    executor: http-node
    claim_producers:
      - name: scarce
        selector: /contended
        intent: rw
        alias: held
    error_types:
      "acquire/unavailable": {action: give_up}
      "scarce/exhausted":    {action: give_up}
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          url:    {type: string, default: "http://recorder:19419/rec/waiting-writer"}
          method: {type: string, default: POST}
```

The node settles on `terminal/error/scarce/exhausted` — the producer's own
class — rather than on a generic acquisition failure. A template can subscribe
to the specific reason this producer refused.
